transcript.statement: Trustworthiness is essential for a library management system, as it ensures that only authenticated members can borrow or return books (TRU-01), which protects user data and prevents unauthorized access. Logging all transactions (TRU-02) guarantees auditability, while enforcing data encryption (TRU-03) secures personal information. Implementing role-based access control (TRU-04) enhances security for librarians and members, and secure mechanisms to manage overdue books (TRU-05) promote accountability. Additionally, allowing members to update personal information securely (TRU-06) fosters trust, and strong password policies (TRU-07) further protect user accounts.

transcript.statement: Responsibility is crucial for ensuring compliance with data protection regulations (RES-01) and promoting fairness (RES-02) in library services. Logging user actions (RES-03) ensures accountability, while enforcing a maximum of 5 books per member (RES-04) supports responsible borrowing. Automatically notifying members of overdue books (RES-05) fosters responsibility, and providing a feedback mechanism (RES-06) allows members to voice concerns, enhancing fairness. An annual report on usage statistics (RES-07) ensures transparency, which is vital for trust and ethical operation.

transcript.statement: Sustainability is vital for the library management system, as it minimizes energy consumption (GRN-01) and promotes responsible resource use. Providing quarterly energy reports (GRN-02) helps track our impact, while digital notifications for overdue books (GRN-03) reduce paper waste. Understanding the carbon footprint of each book (GRN-04) encourages informed choices, and a recycling program for damaged books (GRN-05) supports proper disposal. Tracking energy savings (GRN-06) demonstrates our commitment to efficiency, while prioritizing e-books (GRN-07) reduces physical resource consumption, aligning with sustainability goals.

transcript.statement: Safety and reliability are paramount in a library management system. Ensuring that no member borrows more than 5 books (SAF-01) prevents overloading the system and maintains fair access. Automatic notifications for overdue books (SAF-02) help mitigate risks associated with late returns. Real-time inventory management (SAF-03) is crucial to prevent double borrowing, while a robust backup mechanism (SAF-04) ensures data recovery in case of failures. Revoking privileges for members with overdue books (SAF-05) promotes responsible borrowing. User authentication (SAF-06) ensures only registered members access features, and logging transactions (SAF-07) supports accountability and auditability.

transcript.statement: Performance efficiency is essential for the library management system to ensure optimal user experience. Quick search response times (EFF-01) enhance usability, while allowing up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations (EFF-02) maximizes resource utilization. Real-time tracking of book availability (EFF-03) provides accurate information, and processing returns within 1 second (EFF-04) maintains high throughput. Timely overdue notifications (EFF-05) hold members accountable, and enabling librarians to add/remove books swiftly (EFF-06) ensures efficient inventory management. Maintaining a 99.5% system uptime (EFF-07) guarantees consistent availability for users.

requirements.text: The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations through data encryption for all member data.
The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users to promote fairness and inclusivity.
The system shall log all borrowing transactions for auditability purposes.
The system shall implement a user authentication process to ensure only registered members can access borrowing features.
The system shall automatically notify members of overdue books within 24 hours of the due date.
The system shall enforce a maximum of 5 books per member to ensure fair access.
The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books to prevent double borrowing.
The system shall provide a mechanism to report and manage overdue books securely.
The system shall integrate digital notifications to minimize paper waste.
The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
The system shall allow up to 7 simultaneous book borrow operations per member.
